title: Elastic-net analysis finds limited genomic separation of malaria infections in two connected Amazonian communities
summary: An exploratory preprint applied elastic-net logistic regression to existing genomic data from 47 Plasmodium vivax infections detected in two neighboring Peruvian Amazon communities, including 12 people reporting recent local travel. Repeated nested cross-validation yielded an AUC of 0.625 (95% bootstrap interval 0.522–0.724), versus 0.529 (0.402–0.657) after restricting the sample to non-travelers. This supports a bounded finding that fine-scale assignment was weak and sensitive to sample composition in this dataset. The analyses used different, overlapping infection sets, so their comparison does not isolate a causal effect of travel. Self-reported travel did not establish infection origin; intervals were conditional on saved predictions, and no independent cohort or operational surveillance benefit was tested.
ai_technology: Elastic-net logistic regression with nested cross-validation and K-nearest-neighbor imputation
organization: University of Antwerp; University of Liège; KU Leuven; Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia; Yale University

evidence.tested: Retrospective analysis of 47 infections from two communities; elastic-net classifier evaluated by 20 repetitions of five-fold outer cross-validation with inner tuning. Reported AUC 0.625 overall and 0.529 in a non-traveler subset; infection-level bootstrap intervals retained repeated predictions together.
evidence.unknown: Small and overlapping sample sets; no independent cohort or intervention. Travel was self-reported and did not determine acquisition location. Bootstrap intervals condition on existing predictions without refitting models, and the comparison does not isolate travel as a cause.
evidence.ai_role: A learned penalized classifier measures how much genomic variation distinguishes the two detection communities and how this assignment changes with the analyzed sample composition.

source_review.scope: Research Square v1 full PDF: primary abstract, study setting, modeling, validation and relevant results; no independent reanalysis or experimental pathogen work.
